field:rack::dsp::MidiParser::rotateIndex.finding: P0: the rotate_index setter accepts any int8_t (native/bindings/dsp/midi.cpp:315-316), and Rack's assignChannel trusts the value. In REUSE or ROTATE mode with channels > 1, a value of -2 or below, or 127 (which ++ wraps to -128), makes assignChannel read gates[rotateIndex] at a negative index (Rack-SDK include/dsp/midi.hpp:527-534). It can then return that index as a uint8_t such as 252, and pressNote writes notes, gates, velocities and retriggerPulses at that index (midi.hpp:589). So assign_channel, press_note or process_message after `p.rotate_index = -100` reads and writes outside the parser's arrays. This contradicts the file's stated policy of refusing input that would make Rack index past its arrays. Smallest fix: allow only -1 to MAX_CHANNELS - 1 in the setter (ValueError otherwise; Rack's own invariant: panic sets -1 at midi.hpp:362, and assignChannel keeps it in [0, channels)), document the range in docs/reference/dsp.md#dsp-midi-parser, and add a refusal test.

method:rack::dsp::MidiParser::panic().finding: P1: no cited test calls the parser's panic() binding (native/bindings/dsp/midi.cpp:328). In tests/dsp/in_rack_basic/test_midi.py, Rack's panic runs only inside processCC (the 0x7b message), and the only direct .panic() calls are on MidiGenerator (lines 113 and 343). docs/reference/dsp.md#dsp-midi-parser does not name panic() either. Smallest fix: add a 'panic' op to the parserMethods reference script and its Python replay, or assert that p.panic() clears gates and held_notes but keeps the settings; then mention panic() in the parser section.

method:rack::dsp::MidiParser::processCC(.finding: P0: process_cc's guard (Guard::check, native/bindings/dsp/midi.cpp:218-229) checks the MPE channel only when the message's status is 0x8, 0x9, 0xd, 0xe, or 0xb with note 1. Rack's processCC ignores the status: it switches on getNote(), and for note 0x01 in polyphonic MPE mode it writes mods[msg.getChannel()] (Rack-SDK include/dsp/midi.hpp:462). On MidiParser[2] with channels 2 and MPE_MODE, p.process_cc(message([0xA5, 0x01, 100])) passes the guard and writes mods[5], past the 2-element array. The guard also wrongly refuses a 0xF8 message when clock_division is 0, although processCC never divides (P2). Smallest fix: give process_cc its own check that tests getNote() == 0x01 and the MPE channel against MAX_CHANNELS whatever the status, and drop the clock check for this path; add a test.

method:rack::dsp::MidiParser::processSys.finding: P0: process_system refuses the clock_division == 0 case only when the status is 0xf (native/bindings/dsp/midi.cpp:234). Rack's processSystem ignores the status: it switches on msg.getChannel() alone and evaluates clock % clockDivision for channel 0x8 (Rack-SDK include/dsp/midi.hpp:482, 491). So with p.clock_division = 0, p.process_system(message([0x98, 60, 100])) passes the guard and divides by zero (SIGFPE). The guard also wrongly refuses MPE note messages on channels at or above MAX_CHANNELS, although processSystem never indexes by channel (P2). Smallest fix: give process_system its own check, getChannel() == 0x8 && clockDivision == 0, whatever the status, with no MPE check; add a test with a non-0xF status byte.
